topic: Corals spawn on the same night
script: Once a year, corals on the Great Barrier Reef release their eggs and sperm at almost the same time. This mass spawning usually happens a few nights after a full moon in late spring. Water temperature, moonlight and day length help set the timing. The water fills with floating bundles, like an upside-down snowstorm. Spawning all at once helps eggs and sperm meet in the open ocean. The tiny coral larvae drift for days or weeks before settling to start new corals.
